[Pedagogy review · High priority · missing-prerequisite · pf-2133c7f10b]
In p5-method-block step 3, connect the height of f′ to the tangent gradient of f, including its magnitude. Annotate the right demonstration: after the maximum, downward tangents become steeper then flatter, so f′ falls below zero then rises towards zero. The existing method covers signs and zeros only.

[Pedagogy review · High priority · missing-prerequisite · pf-f782d08c16]
The sketching exercise introduces unbounded tangent gradients and vertical endpoint tangents without teaching their consequences for the derivative.
Before p10-q9-c add: “As positive tangent gradients grow without bound, f'(x) rises without bound; as negative tangent gradients grow in magnitude without bound, f'(x) falls without bound. A vertical tangent has no finite derivative.” At p10-q9-g demonstrate with three tangents approaching the origin from the right: “Their positive gradients grow without bound. The derivative is defined only for x>0 and rises without bound near 0.”
Also affects: p10-q9-f, p10-q9-g, p10-q9-h, p10-q9-i

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · extension · pf-5ea755777e]
At p7-q6: Add (e) “Let g(x)=f(x)+3. Sketch g'(x).” Answer: the same sketch as in (d), with zeros at -1 and 1. (f) “Let h(x)=-f(x). Sketch h'(x).” Answer: reflect the sketch from (d) in the x-axis; negative outside [-1,1], positive between -1 and 1, and zero at both endpoints. (g) “Why does adding 3 leave the derivative unchanged?” Answer: vertical translation does not change tangent gradients.

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · variation-sequence · pf-6cc7db0f36]
At p18-q15-root: Add the single instruction “Predict before calculating.” Add (e) y=x²-4x-5; (f) y=x²-4x; (g) y=x²-4x+9; followed by (h) y=x²+4x+9. Answers for (e)–(g): y'=2x-4, increasing for x>2. Answer for (h): y'=2x+4, increasing for x>-2.

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · extension · pf-dac1c69450]
At p17-q13-root: Add (d) “How many real solutions does f(x)=3 have?” Answer: three. (e) “How many distinct real solutions does f(x)=1 have?” Answer: two, x=-1 and x=2. (f) “How many real solutions does f(x)=6 have?” Answer: one.
